svg.text: Anti-slop pilot: what the analyzers actually produced
mypy-multi-agent @ 9f9ca93 · 12,473 production TS lines (src + shared + web) · 7 analyzers · 2026-10-27
129 adjudications over 109 distinct findings; 20 were read in both passes by different models. 534 findings were never read at all.
71% of the verified population is duplication nobody should fix.
344 of ~484. Precision was never the constraint — jscpd was 91% precise and every clone was test boilerplate. The defensible density is 11.2 actionable findings per 1,000 lines.
gate — format and style; every finding in test/
gate — 62 ms, the only tool reporting in scripts/ and web/
gate — clean over src / test / shared
keep dead-code + cognitive_crap; drop crap, cognitive, unused_files
keep types only; files/exports/binaries are entry-point cascades
the 81% is borrowed: its own ai-slop engine verifies 2 of 5
drop — precise and worthless; 246 of 376 clones in test/
“verified” = the reading confirmed the claimed problem exists. It says nothing about whether the finding is worth fixing.
A spawned bin, a vitest config, a README-documented script
and 50 web/ files all read as dead code. The rule cannot
see how a file is launched.
crap and cognitive scored flat guard chains at 10–18. Zero
of eight held when the code was read: no nesting, one
aislop's 81% rides on rules oxlint, ruff and jscpd already
run. Its own ai-slop engine — the flagship — verifies 2 of
No labelled defect set exists, so this is what the tools emit — not what defects exist. 563 findings were never read.
One repo, 12.5k lines. Nothing here shows the tools prevent slop, only what they report when run.
It produced the best findings of the run; the unguided-vs-guided comparison is prose, not a score.
